public_rationale: Zitron says there is nothing after generative AI and no other hypergrowth markets in tech. In context, he means markets that could carry the growth of Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and public software firms. He gives no growth rate, size threshold or timeframe. 'Nothing else after' is also partly an open-ended forecast. Any test would need an invented threshold. A small, fast-growing niche would stretch the claim against him, and a big-tech-scale bar would be the evaluator's own construction. The result would depend on that choice, not on his words. So the claim cannot be fairly graded.
limitations: Under a stricter, explicit definition, a future market could test the forward-looking part, but the speaker did not supply one.

'Hypergrowth market' has no stated growth rate or size threshold. 'Nothing else after' also looks forward with no deadline.

Small-scale fast growth, such as robotaxi rides, would not fairly test a claim about markets able to carry tech-industry growth. A size-and-growth threshold would have to be invented, and the result would turn on that choice.
criteria.support_condition: Not scoreable. It would need an agreed definition of a hypergrowth market big enough to carry big-tech growth.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not scoreable for the same reason. Any counterexample depends on a threshold the speaker did not give.
